questions.question: The points (P-1, P + 2), (P, P + 1), (P + 1, P) are collinear if:
questions.questionHtml: The points (P-1, P + 2), (P, P + 1), (P + 1, P) are collinear if:
questions.solution:
Method-1

Points:
A(P − 1, P + 2)
B(P, P + 1)
C(P + 1, P)

For collinear points:

Slope AB = Slope BC

Slope AB
= ( (P + 1) − (P + 2) ) / ( P − (P − 1) )
= (−1) / 1
= −1

Slope BC
= ( P − (P + 1) ) / ( (P + 1) − P )
= (−1) / 1
= −1

Since Slope AB = Slope BC, the points lie on the same straight line.

Answer: Points are collinear for all values of P.

Method-2

Using the Shoelace Method (Area of triangle = 0 for collinear points)

Points:
A(P − 1, P + 2)
B(P, P + 1)
C(P + 1, P)

Area condition:

½ | x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂) | = 0

Substitute values:

= ½ | (P − 1)[(P + 1) − P] + P[P − (P + 2)] + (P + 1)[(P + 2) − (P + 1)] |

= ½ | (P − 1)(1) + P(−2) + (P + 1)(1) |

= ½ | P − 1 − 2P + P + 1 |

= ½ | 0 |

= 0

Area = 0 ⇒ Points are collinear

Answer: Points are collinear for all values of P.

questions.solution:
Let the numbers be 12x and 12y

Since HCF = 12,
so x and y are co-prime

Using formula:

LCM = HCF × x × y

720 = 12 × x × y

x × y = 60

Prime factorization:

60 = 2² × 3 × 5

Number of distinct primes = 3

Here 3 Unique Prime Numbers (UPN), therefore 4 pairs are possible.

Possible (x, y):

(1,60), (3,20), (4,15), (5,12)

Numbers:

(12,720), (36,240), (48,180), (60,144)

Therefore, 4 pairs are possible.
